question: Which of the following is a hydroxybenzaldehyde that possesses a hydroxy substituent at position 2 extracted from the herb 'meadow sweet'?
solution:
The correct answer is **Salicylaldehyde**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Salicylaldehyde**:

 
 
• Formula: C7H6O2
 
• Hydroxybenzaldehyde: It possesses a hydroxy substituent (-OH) at position 2 on the benzene ring.
 
• Source: It is extracted from the herb 'meadow sweet' and is a key component in the synthesis of aspirin.
 
 
 
• **Cinnamaldehyde**:
 
 
• Formula: C9H8O
 
• Structure: It is a compound with a benzene ring and an unsaturated aldehyde group. Derived from cinnamon bark.
 
 
 
• **Acetaldehyde**:
 
 
• Formula: C2H4O
 
• Structure: It is a simple aldehyde, not a hydroxybenzaldehyde.
 
 
 
• **Formaldehyde**:
 
 
• Formula: CH2O
 
• Structure: It is the simplest aldehyde, not a hydroxybenzaldehyde.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Salicylaldehyde in Meadowsweet**:

 
 
• Meadow sweet (Filipendula ulmaria) is a plant from which salicylaldehyde can be extracted.
 
• This compound has anti-inflammatory properties and has historical significance in herbal medicine.
 
 
 
• **Salicylaldehyde in Aspirin Synthesis**:
 
 
• Salicylaldehyde is a precursor in the synthesis of salicylic acid, which is then used to produce aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid).
 
• Aspirin is a widely used medication with analgesic (pain-relieving), antipyretic (fever-reducing), and anti-inflammatory properties.
